title: Security guards paid outside the bid: after one contract ended, and on a “temporary” award

beats.text: San Francisco kept paying two security-guard firms outside a current bid. How much?

visual.label: Security guards
visual.sub: paid outside a current competed contract, 2022 to 2026

beats.text: 6,234,446 dollars.

visual.label: dollars paid to two guard firms outside a current competed contract
visual.sub: ABA Protection and Black Bear Security

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The City buys guards through citywide contracts, put out to bid.

visual.label: Office of Contract Administration
visual.sub: bids and holds the citywide guard contracts

beats.text: The first lead: ABA Protection’s bid contract ended on 31 December 2022.
642,889 dollars of it was never used.
Yet the payments went on. How much more?
1,735,492 dollars, with no contract number.

visual.label: paid to ABA Protection with no contract number

beats.text: The second lead: the Public Utilities Commission placed 60 small orders with the firm.
30 were for exactly 9,262.40 dollars.

visual.label: Public Utilities Commission orders to ABA Protection

beats.text: 24 were for exactly 9,724.40.

visual.label: Public Utilities Commission orders to ABA Protection

beats.text: Each sat just under the 10,000 dollar cap for buying with no bid.

visual.label: Public Utilities Commission orders to ABA Protection

beats.text: The City’s purchasing rules bar splitting an order “under any circumstances”.
And 23 of the orders came after the Commission’s own new bid guard contracts began.

visual.fromLab: bid guard contracts with Treeline Security begin

beats.text: The third lead:

visual.text: Authority: NO OTHER SOURCE · no contract number · $810,964

beats.text: Public Health paid the firm 810,964 dollars on two orders marked “no other source”.

visual.text: Authority: NO OTHER SOURCE · no contract number · $810,964

beats.text: Yet its own replacement guard contracts, with another firm, began in February 2023.

visual.text: Authority: NO OTHER SOURCE · no contract number · $810,964

beats.text: Sole source means no other supplier could do it. Yet the City bought guards from 8 firms.

visual.label: “No other source”
visual.sub: guards bought from 8 firms under competed contracts

beats.text: The fourth lead: Black Bear Security took over guarding a Real Estate Division site in August 2022.
The award is recorded as a temporary purchase, after a contractor failed to deliver.
Temporary? It ran four years. How much was paid on it?
4,498,953 dollars.

visual.label: paid on Black Bear’s “temporary” contract
visual.sub: the earlier contract for the site paid $347,794

beats.text: Citywide, 77% of all payments under that label are this one contract.

visual.label: of payments under the “failure to deliver” label since fiscal 2019

beats.text: The fifth lead: against the City’s other guard firms, these two stand apart.

visual.label: Share of City money outside a competed contract, eight guard firms

beats.text: Six of eight firms had at most 15% of their City money outside a competed contract.

visual.label: Share of City money outside a competed contract, eight guard firms

beats.text: ABA had 46%. Black Bear, 44%.

visual.label: Share of City money outside a competed contract, eight guard firms

beats.text: ABA’s only registered San Francisco address is 101 Grove Street, Public Health’s central office.

visual.text: 101 Grove St, opened 3 November 2020; business name “Health Department”

beats.text: That is most likely its work site, but it is the City’s own building.

visual.text: 101 Grove St, opened 3 November 2020; business name “Health Department”

beats.text: Nothing shows a guard post left unstaffed, or a price above the contract rate.

beats.text: What would settle it? The contract office’s files, and the invoices behind each order.

A lead is a question, not an accusation.
